main_body: Gong frame: two wooden posts with a top crossbeam and base feet, holding a round golden gong. The gong is hung on two cords.
top_band: Column x=16 reads: row 2 light pink-brown (L137, 1 row), row 3 mid brown (L105), rows 4-5 dark brown (L49). Below that is the gong, with no distinct top surface.
evidence: The crossbeam is a straight front view. Only a 1-row highlight at row 2 marks its top, so it is a rim and not a top surface. The posts are plain vertical strips (x=23 is one L=92 run, rows 12-20), with no top faces visible. The base feet have a 1-row light edge at row 29 over dark rows, which is also only a rim. The gong is a flat disc seen face-on. The frame's horizontal beams and base do not show top faces, so this is a front elevation and fails the frame rule.

style.evidence: The gong has about 5 gold steps (L 128, 160, 194, 224) with a highlight swirl and a darker lower rim, so it is shaded with care. The wood has about 3-4 steps and the outlines lean brown, not neutral black (0% near-neutral edge pixels). There are no flat fills (0% coverage). Distinct colours (18 vs 38-40) and colours per tile (11 vs 17-20) are below the references, but not by a wide margin. The piece is simple but not sticker-like, and a careful artist could accept it next to the references.
